note: Midships inboard profile at z = +0.65 m, starboard of centreline, cut through the centre of a stringer void. Principal characteristics are Sunseeker's published figures; profiles are derived from them and are marked as assumptions where they are not.

profiles._note: 11 samples at u = 0.0 (transom) to 1.0 (stem). Linear interpolation between samples. keelLift is the fraction of the draft by which the keel is lifted above its lowest point: 0 at the deepest station, 1 at the ends. ASSUMED — replace with yard lines plan.

levels._note: Vertical levels above the baseline (y = 0 at the lowest point of the keel). ASSUMED.

bulkheads._note: Transverse positions, x in metres from midships (negative aft). ASSUMED.

faults.note: Condensation in the forward stringer void. The money fault: invisible to the hull-side capacitance meter, and the space is only reachable through the deck.
Water ingress over the engine bay. Distinguishable from condensation only by the time series.
Fuel vapour. The safety gate: a person should not enter to confirm it.
Hot bearing on the port engine.

assumptions: Transverse bulkhead positions are assumed from the layout description and are NOT from a lines plan.
Deck and deckhead heights are assumed from general arrangement and are NOT from a lines plan.

The cut plane at z = +0.65 m is chosen to pass through the centre of a stringer void; the actual stringer positions are NOT known. The cut plane leaves the hull forward of about x = 6.9 m, which is why the forward void stops there.
Inspection hatch positions and clear widths are assumed. The existence, size and location of any deck hatch on this class is unknown and is question A2 for the marine engineer.
The void under the main deck is treated as one continuous volume. On a real boat the transverse floors divide it into bays, which changes the access graph.
The crawler diameter is assumed. It is the parameter that decides whether a deck hatch is a route or a wall.
